proposal.summary: The requester (SH-CS) framed the issue as slow ticket handling and asked for an AI agent to auto-answer disputes and auto-fix billing (CL-01). Investigation (PD-1) instead established the root problem as: dispute volume genuinely doubled from ~600/month to 1180-1260/month starting August (E-06), driven predominantly by disputes on ACTUAL (not estimated) meter reads (E-01), with tariff change (E-02) and SLA breach (E-03) ruled out. The best-supported mechanism is a billing-import rejection effect (E-11), localizing the defect to AMI data quality or a billing-import rule change rather than ticket-handling speed or AMI delivery failure. The release ships only the DA-ROUTE-related work (quantifying the route-completion/dispute link and a possible route-priority update), gated by SH-FIELD's required human confirmation (K-DISPATCH); no billing-rule investigation, no vendor MDMS access request, and no automated bill writes (K-BILLWRITE) are included. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with nothing held back, because the DEFINE gate only conditionally passed and several verification obligations remain open or deferred rather than fully resolved.
key_points: Root problem (PD-1): dispute tickets doubled since August (E-06), dominated by disputes on ACTUAL-read bills (1785) over ESTIMATED-read bills (1240) (E-01); tariff change ruled out (E-02) and ticket response times are within SLA (E-03), so the originally requested 'response-speed' framing (CL-01, SH-CS) was tested and rejected (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING, contradicted by E-01, E-03, E-04, E-07).

Mechanism was localized using E-11: among AMI-channel reads behind disputed ESTIMATED bills, 1184 were delivered and exported but rejected under a billing-import HIGH_CONSUMPTION flag, versus only 56 with no read at all - this led to VOB-U-MECHANISM-LOCUS being RESOLVED (seq196) and the AMI-delivery-failure hypothesis H-AMI-DATA-DELIVERY being REJECTED, leaving H-AMI-METER-DATA-QUALITY and H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE SUPPORTED.

Field route completion was 88% against a 95% target across 9200 manual-read accounts (E-04), a real but partial shortfall; SH-FIELD attributes this to a staffing shortfall (E-07, CL-03), but this is an unverified stakeholder claim from a party with a contract-headcount incentive, and H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE remains only a CANDIDATE hypothesis, not confirmed.

The release scope (SD-1) covers only DA-ROUTE actions: quantifying the route-completion/dispute link and, if warranted, a route-priority update (push_route_update) - the latter requires SH-FIELD's runtime confirmation per K-DISPATCH (service contract §4.2, E-08) and was in fact blocked pending VOB-R-3 (protected_action_blocked, seq176).

Billing-rule-log review, vendor MDMS access escalation, and cross-referencing disputed actual-read bills (SR-R1, SR-R2, SR-R3) are not part of this release scope; any eventual bill correction must go through manual Billing Operations action under K-BILLWRITE, not automated writes.

Release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with an empty hold list, following a DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS where deferred items were tracked as VOBs, and a verify step (seq205) that passed layer-1 checks but failed one semantic check.

VOB-U-TICKET-CLOSURE-VS-BILL-ACCUR remains OPEN (whether cutting ticket volume via faster responses could mask unresolved billing inaccuracy) but is outside this release's scope; VOB-R-3 (route-shortfall contribution and E-07 accuracy) is OPEN and intersects the release scope non-critically.
